question: Which nitrogen form dominates the char of sawdust pyrolysed at 500 °C, and at what N 1s binding energy does the paper place that form?
trap: N-A at 399.7 eV or N-5 at 400.3 eV
rendered:
According to the document, at 500 °C, the char of sawdust (SD) pyrolyzed at 500 °C (denoted as SD500) has a dominant nitrogen form of N-6, with a relative content of 43% (as shown in Fig. 4b). 

The N 1s binding energy for pyridinic nitrogen (N-6) is 398.7 ± 0.3 eV.
